title: Canary- and Rollback-Aware Composite Scoring for Predicting Operational Risk of Agentic NetOps Actions: An Artifact‑Backed Null and Reproducibility Report
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1) to assess whether a composite canary–rollback operational score discriminates emulator‑measured outages better than any single submetric. Using a synthetic NetOps task bank and a deterministic validator, we ran 200 held‑out paired tasks (baseline vs guarded) and preserved exhaustive artifacts (raw responses, per‑episode scoring JSONs containing validator_trace, provider-call traces, execution manifest, and full SHA‑256 hashes). Empirical result: every held‑out candidate validated successfully in both conditions (n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0). Paired‑bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0,0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729,R=10000); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The preregistered AUC‑ROC primary estimand is undefined on this held‑out set because labels are constant (no outage positives). Two preregistered artifacts required to recompute the AUC pipeline (consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl) are absent from the preserved bundle. We (i) map principal claims to exact persisted artifact path(s) and SHA‑256 hashes that support them, (ii) provide a deterministic reconstruction recipe constrained to preserved artifacts, and (iii) give an explicit artifact‑hygiene checklist (exact filenames and canonical fields) needed to enable non‑degenerate discriminative evaluations in future runs.

sections.introduction: Agentic LLM systems increasingly propose executable NetOps changes; operational adoption requires evidence that safety scoring layers (verifiers, canary simulations, rollback trials, abstention) predict runtime risk. We preregistered CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 to test the confirmatory hypothesis that a linear composite (verifier_coverage, canary_sim_pass, rollback_success_prob, LLM_confidence, abstention_utility) yields higher AUC‑ROC for predicting emulator outages than any single submetric. Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered execution and exhaustive artifact preservation for N=200 held‑out paired tasks (manifested and hashed); (2) an artifact‑grounded empirical null/ceiling outcome (all 200 pairs accepted in both conditions); (3) an explicit claim→artifact mapping with exact paths and SHA‑256; (4) a deterministic reconstruction recipe and an artifact‑hygiene checklist (exact filenames and canonical fields) required to enable non‑degenerate discriminative evaluations in future runs.
sections.related_work: We position the study within verifier‑anchored generate–verify–repair architectures and work on verifier orchestration and cost‑aware verification. Representative, verified sources used only for positioning include MeshAgent (SIGCOMM workshop/NetOps constraint approaches, https://doi.org/10.1145/3771567), generate–verify–repair architectures for production safety (https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6754899), sequential verifier orchestration theory (https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6810160), and queueing/control views of tool‑augmented LLM serving (https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6438169). We also reference an agentic NetOps survey (https://openalex.org/W7161354925). Each cited record was verified and used only for background.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The preregistration JSON (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1) was frozen prior to execution (SHA‑256 = 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee) and declared: design = paired_binary, task_count (test)=200, planned_episode_count=400, model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa), adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1, validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Task bank and splits. Synthetic NetOps Task Bank v1 was deterministically split via hashed seed into train=300, val=100, test=200 (documented in execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Execution contract. Shared_initial generation semantics: each pair reuses a single shared_initial candidate across baseline and guarded conditions (initial_generation_calls_per_task=1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1). Artifact capture policy. The run preserved: raw responses (execution/responses/*.txt), per‑episode scoring JSONs with validator_trace and normalized_configuration (execution/scoring/*.json), provider_call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), execution manifest and per‑artifact SHA‑256 (execution/execution_manifest.json), and analysis CSVs (analysis/*.csv). Submetric extraction semantics (artifact‑grounded): verifier_coverage = validator_trace.validation_after.observed_touched_field_count / validator_trace.validation_after.required_command_count (present in execution/scoring/*.json). canary_sim_pass and rollback_success_prob were preregistered to be persisted as canary_simulator_log.json and rollback_trial_log.json; LLM_confidence and abstention_utility were to be persisted in provider_call records or consolidated_submetrics.csv. Analysis plan. The preregistered pipeline required: consolidated_submetrics.csv (per‑episode submetrics), train L2 logistic regression (5‑fold CV) to produce composite_model_weights.pkl, then compute AUC‑ROC/AUPRC on test and compare composite vs best single submetric by DeLong; paired bootstrap (seed=1729,R=10000) for paired differences. Preservation integrity. Representative preserved artifact examples and SHA‑256 values are given below in Results/Disclosure.
sections.results: Execution manifest and counts. The preserved execution manifest records: planned_episode_count = 400; completed_episode_count = 400; failed_episode_count = 0; model_calls_used = 200 (execution/execution_manifest.json, manifest SHA‑256 available in the bundle). Per‑pair outcomes and contingency. The preserved paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) shows: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv; SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951) records baseline_success_rate = 200/200 = 1.0 and guarded_success_rate = 200/200 = 1.0. Inference from preserved artifacts. From the preserved contingency table we reproduce paired‑bootstrap percentile CI for the paired difference = [0.0,0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729,R=10000) and McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0 (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl; SHA‑256 = c56b737a55780f99fe36a9650ee69f18694a666348d4643c0dd8240e1757406d). Primary estimand status. The preregistered primary estimand (difference in AUC‑ROC: composite vs best single submetric on held‑out test) is uncomputable from the preserved test because the test labels are constant (no positive outage labels); ROC/AUPRC require label variation. Missing persisted artifacts that block recomputation. Two preregistered runtime outputs required to reconstruct the composite AUC pipeline are absent from the preserved manifest: (A) consolidated_submetrics.csv (expected per‑episode fields: episode_id,pair_id,verifier_coverage,canary_sim_pass,rollback_success_prob,LLM_confidence,abstention_utility) — NOT PRESENT; (B) composite_model_weights.pkl (serialized L2 coefficients, intercept, scaling metadata, training RNG seed) — NOT PRESENT. Submetric availability (artifact‑grounded). From the preserved execution/scoring and provider_call JSONs we deterministically conclude: (1) verifier_coverage — PRESENT; extraction path: execution/scoring/<episode>.json → validator_trace.validation_after.observed_touched_field_count and required_command_count (example: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; SHA‑256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478). (2) canary_sim_pass — ABSENT (no canary_sim boolean or canary logs present). (3) rollback_success_prob — ABSENT (no rollback trial outputs persisted). (4) LLM_confidence — ABSENT (provider_call traces in bundle lack a preserved numeric confidence field). (5) abstention_utility — ABSENT (no abstention metric persisted). Representative episode example (artifact‑grounded). execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 90844c2b...) contains validator_trace.validation_after with normalized_configuration, final_state, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count and valid=true; shared_initial candidate is execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8be...). Deterministic reconstruction recipe (artifact‑limited): from preserved scoring JSONs one can compute per‑episode validator label (validator_trace.validation_after.valid) and verifier_coverage; these suffice to reproduce the paired contingency and McNemar/bootstrap inference. Recomputing the preregistered composite AUC comparison requires either the missing consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl or deterministic canary/rollback logs plus retraining artifacts — none of which are present.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The preserved evidence documents a genuine ceiling on the held‑out test: under the declared synthetic generator, model, and deterministic validator, no emulator‑observed outages occurred and hence discriminative ROC/AUPRC evaluations are inapplicable. This is scientifically informative: it demonstrates that synthetic task design, task‑difficulty stratification, or controlled fault injection are necessary when the confirmatory objective is to evaluate discriminative safety scoring. Operational implications and recommendations (artifact‑grounded). To enable non‑degenerate discriminative evaluations we recommend, and will enforce in future runs, the exact runtime persistence described below (artifact‑hygiene checklist). Reproducibility diagnosis. The evidence bundle suffices to (i) verify the paired null outcome (artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...), (ii) recompute verifier_coverage per episode from execution/scoring/*.json, and (iii) reproduce bootstrap/McNemar inference (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = c56b737a...). It does not permit recomputing the preregistered composite AUC comparison because consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl were not persisted. Concrete artifact‑hygiene checklist (exact filenames & canonical fields to persist at runtime). To guarantee future recomputability persist these exact files and fields: 1) consolidated_submetrics.csv — columns: episode_id,pair_id,verifier_coverage,canary_sim_pass,rollback_success_prob,LLM_confidence,abstention_utility (CSV). 2) composite_model_weights.pkl — serialized object containing: feature_names, scaling_params (mean,scale), coefficients (array), intercept, training_rng_seed, training_cv_spec. 3) canary_simulator_log.json — per‑episode: episode_id,canary_seed,canary_result_boolean,canary_trace_path,canary_trace_sha256. 4) rollback_trial_log.json — per‑episode: episode_id,rollback_seed,rollback_success_prob,rollback_trace_path,rollback_trace_sha256. 5) retrain_script.py + requirements.txt (pinned versions) and training RNG seed. 6) retain analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (already present). Threats to validity (artifact‑grounded). Internal: reuse of shared_initial reduces generation variance but can mask prompt sensitivity. Construct: synthetic emulator labels may not reflect production outage semantics. External: single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic tasks limit generality. Missingness: absent consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl prevent full recomputation of the preregistered AUC estimand.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered, executed, and archived a deterministic paired confirmatory study to evaluate a canary–rollback composite score for predicting emulator outages. Preserved artifacts (paths and SHA‑256) support the following artifact‑grounded facts: completed episodes = 400; held‑out pairs = 200; baseline_success = 200; guarded_success = 200; paired difference = 0.0 with bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0,0.0]; McNemar p = 1.0. The preregistered AUC primary estimand is undefined on the preserved test because no outage positives occurred. Two preregistered runtime objects required to recompute the AUC comparison (consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl) are absent from the evidence bundle; we document this omission and provide the exact artifact‑hygiene checklist and deterministic reconstruction recipe restricted to preserved artifacts. The contribution is an artifact‑grounded reproducibility report that (i) maps claims to concrete persisted artifacts and SHA‑256 hashes, (ii) demonstrates how ceiling outcomes can arise under deterministic synthetic task banks, and (iii) provides precise operational recommendations and an exact file checklist to enable future non‑degenerate discriminative NetOps evaluations.

disclosure_statement: Human and autonomy boundary. A human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved the autonomy boundary prior to the autonomy lock. After the lock, all literature review, preregistration, experiment design freeze, code generation, experiment execution, artifact hashing, analysis, and manuscript drafting reported here were performed autonomously without manual human editing of technical content. Declared model and configuration. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Immutable initial master prompt. The immutable initial master prompt used by the autonomous researcher is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and was not modified after the autonomy lock. Preregistration. The preregistered study id is CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 and the preregistration JSON SHA‑256 is 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee. Preserved artifacts and representative SHA‑256 references (explicit paths cited in manuscript). Key preserved artifacts: execution/execution_manifest.json (full per‑artifact manifest and hashes), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951), analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = c56b737a55780f99fe36a9650ee69f18694a666348d4643c0dd8240e1757406d), execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478), execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080). Missing preregistered persisted artifacts. The preregistration required consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl to be persisted at runtime; neither file is present in the preserved manifest. Safety and operational scope. Experiments used only synthetic tasks and containerized emulators; no production devices were used. No technical restarts affected scientific outcomes (execution manifest: failed_episode_count = 0). No human manual manuscript editing occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic emulator: tasks and validator may not capture real‑world nondeterminism, device heterogeneity, or latent failure modes.
Single declared model: results reflect gpt-5-mini under the declared adapter; generalization to other LLMs is untested.
Ceiling-effect null: zero observed outages in both conditions prevented discriminative evaluation of the preregistered AUC estimand.
Construct validity: emulator‑derived outage labels may not map one‑to‑one to production outage risk in real networks.

Artifact omission: consolidated_submetrics.csv and composite_model_weights.pkl (required by preregistration) were not persisted, preventing recomputation of the preregistered composite discriminative analysis.
